# ReShiki 0.14.0

This release names structures with a new offline engine that says whether each
name is the preferred IUPAC name, adds Fischer projections and IUPAC drawing
conventions, and ships the first `reshiki` Python package.

- **Chemical names:** structure to name runs on a Rust port of openclatura, and
  every name must parse back to the same structure. Each name is tagged
  **Preferred IUPAC name**, **Systematic name, not the preferred IUPAC name** or
  **Systematic name, preference not verified**, with the reason on hover. Salts,
  isotopologues, radicals, ring assemblies, phane, spiro, r/s, endo/exo and
  (M)/(P) names are new, and many names follow the IUPAC 2013 rules more closely.
- **Name import:** reads salts, phane names, signed CIP names, peptide and glycan
  symbols on OPSIN's current main branch. **Look up online…** asks PubChem for
  common names after you confirm each query. Names copy as rich text.
- **Stereochemistry:** Fischer projections with D/L, **Invert Configuration
  Here**, (M)/(P) axes, steroid α/β labels, Ξ/ξ for unknown configuration and
  stereo checks in **Check drawing**.
- **Drawing conventions:** IUPAC double-bond placement, wedge direction, charge
  and radical order, partial charges, salt layout, bracket superscripts, D/T
  isotope labels and two-sided amino-acid residue groups.
- **Templates:** steroids, nucleosides, Fischer projections, coordination
  geometry frames and 9H purines, found by IUPAC names.
- **3D models and crystals:** **Structure changed · Update model**, regenerated
  conformers, 3D atom labels, ORTEP thermal ellipsoids, and Repeat and Look
  along in the 3D crystal view.
- **Python package:** `uv add reshiki` draws, converts and analyzes structures
  from scripts, Jupyter, pandas and Excel with the editor's engine.
- **Browser editor:** touch drawing, pinch zoom and long-press menus; Save
  writes back to the opened file in Chrome and Edge.

**File compatibility:** most drawings saved by 0.14.0 still use document format
30 and open in 0.13.1. Drawings with a custom reaction-label gap, ORTEP
settings, a 3D model generated in 0.14.0 or a two-sided residue group use
formats 31–34, which 0.13.1 cannot open. Older drawings still open in 0.14.0.
Keep a copy saved by an older version if you share files with someone who
uses it.

**Known limits:** a CXSMILES wedge flag on a `/` or `\` bond drops the stated
E/Z, and MOL files keep an atropisomer axis only where the 2D drawing can show
it ([Known limits](https://reshiki.com/developer/changes-0.14/#known-limits)).

macOS release downloads are signed and notarized. Windows and Linux downloads
remain unsigned; Windows production signing is pending.
